notes: Action catalogue. Every action the player can pick, with time cost, effect and when it is correct.
Effect types are a fixed set implemented in code: scene, reveal_state, reveal_findings, ask, intervene, set_pose, tag, waste.
correctWhen uses the condition language in content/FORMAT.md. Time costs are placeholders to tune in play-testing.

listedForCasualty is true when the action appears in the casualty's expected.lifeSavingInterventions or expected.keyActions. Use it for presentation-specific help (glucose, inhaler) so authors decide where it applies.
onTrue.keepPoseWithAid: when the casualty has a mobility_aid of one of these types, keep their pose (a wheelchair user moves in their chair) and only add the motion overlay.
Card templates don't include the time: every card entry is timestamped when it is written.

groups.trap: Plausible but wrong in an MCI sieve

actions.label: Put on gloves
actions.feedbackWrong: You already had gloves on.

actions.label: Call out: "If you can walk or get yourself over here, come to me"
Withdraw to safety
actions.feedbackWrong: Nothing on scene required withdrawing, so you lost time and left casualties untriaged.

actions.label: Drop, cover and hold
actions.feedbackWrong: Nothing was shaking or falling, so taking cover cost time.

actions.label: Make the area safe (stop traffic, cones, isolate the hazard)
actions.feedbackWrong: There was no hazard you could make safe, so this cost time.

actions.label: Radio a METHANE report
actions.feedbackWrong: One METHANE report is enough; repeat it only when something changes.

actions.label: Ask them to make their own way to the collection point
actions.feedbackWrong: They could not follow the request (unresponsive or trapped), so asking cost time without telling you anything new.

actions.label: Open the airway (head tilt, chin lift)
actions.feedbackWrong: They were talking or breathing without help, so the airway was already open.

actions.label: Look, listen and feel for breathing; count the rate
Give a simple command ("squeeze my hand")
Give 5 rescue breaths
actions.feedbackWrong: Rescue breaths in the sieve are only for a child who is still not breathing after the airway is opened but has a pulse.

actions.label: Ask name and age
actions.feedbackWrong: They could not talk, so asking cost time. "Unknown" is a valid entry.

actions.label: Ask what happened
actions.feedbackWrong: They could not talk, so asking cost time. Use the scene briefing or a bystander.

actions.label: Ask about allergies, medications and medical history
actions.feedbackWrong: Allergies, medications and history belong in re-triage or just before handover, not the first sweep.

actions.label: Reassure them briefly: help is coming
actions.feedbackWrong: They could not hear or respond; reassurance can wait for someone who can.

actions.label: Get a bystander to hold pressure on the wound
actions.feedbackWrong: There was either no bystander to help or no bleed that needed pressure.

actions.label: Move on to the next casualty
actions.feedbackWrong: Tag the casualty before moving on, so the next team knows their priority.

actions.label: Apply a tourniquet
actions.feedbackWrong: A tourniquet only helps a catastrophic bleed on an arm or leg. Pack and press on junctional bleeds.

actions.label: Apply firm direct pressure
actions.feedbackWrong: Only a catastrophic bleed needs you to stop and press during the sieve. Minor bleeding can wait.

actions.label: Pack the wound and press
actions.feedbackWrong: Packing is for catastrophic bleeds where a tourniquet won't fit (groin, neck, armpit). On a limb a tourniquet is faster.

actions.label: Ask them to press firmly on their own wound
actions.feedbackWrong: Self-pressure only works for a major bleed in someone who can follow instructions. A catastrophic bleed needs you.

actions.label: Give them something sugary to eat or drink
actions.feedbackWrong: Sugar by mouth is only for a known low blood sugar in someone awake enough to swallow safely. Never give anything by mouth to a drowsy or confused casualty.

actions.label: Help them use their own reliever inhaler
actions.feedbackWrong: Only helpful for someone with asthma who has their own reliever and can still follow instructions.

actions.label: Put them in the recovery position
actions.feedbackWrong: The recovery position is for someone who is breathing (on their own or once the airway is opened) but only responds to pain or not at all. They were awake, not breathing, or trapped.

actions.label: Start CPR
actions.feedbackWrong: In an MCI, someone not breathing after one airway attempt is tagged dead. CPR ties a rescuer to one casualty while others who could be saved wait.

actions.label: Splint the injured limb
actions.feedbackWrong: Splinting is good first aid but not part of the sieve. Tag and move on; treatment teams splint later.

actions.label: Give them a drink of water
actions.feedbackWrong: Injured casualties may need surgery or may vomit; nothing by mouth. It also costs time.

actions.label: Do a full head-to-toe check
actions.feedbackWrong: A full survey finds everything but takes minutes. The sieve needs only walking, breathing, circulation and commands.

actions.label: Take a detailed history
actions.feedbackWrong: A detailed history belongs to the treatment area, not the first sweep.

actions.label: Lift the debris off and pull them free
actions.feedbackWrong: Releasing a long-trapped casualty without medical support can cause sudden collapse (crush syndrome). Flag them for medical before release.

actions.label: Flag for medical before release
actions.feedbackWrong: They were not trapped, so there was nothing to flag.

actions.label: Stay with them and keep them company
actions.feedbackWrong: Kind, but every minute here is a minute another casualty waits to be triaged.

actions.label: Drag them to a safer spot
actions.feedbackWrong: Moving a casualty without an immediate hazard risks worsening injuries and takes you away from the sieve.

actions.label: Pull out the impaled object
actions.feedbackWrong: Never remove an impaled object; it may be plugging a major bleed. Pad around it and leave it.

actions.label: Apply a cervical collar
actions.feedbackWrong: Spinal care is not part of the sieve; note the mechanism and move on.

actions.label: Cool the burn with running water
actions.feedbackWrong: Cooling is correct first aid but takes 20 minutes. In the sieve, tag and get a walking wounded or treatment team to cool.

actions.label: Wrap them in a blanket
actions.feedbackWrong: Warmth matters, but it comes after the sieve. Ask a walking wounded or bystander to do it.

actions.label: Search their pockets for ID
actions.feedbackWrong: "Unknown" is a valid entry. Searching for ID costs time you need for the sieve.

actions.label: Measure blood pressure
actions.feedbackWrong: Blood pressure isn't part of the sieve; radial pulse and capillary refill tell you enough.

actions.label: Clean and dress the cuts
actions.feedbackWrong: Minor wounds wait. Only catastrophic bleeding is treated during the sieve.

actions.label: Call your mum
actions.feedbackWrong: She'd be proud you volunteered, but maybe call after the exercise.

actions.label: Check your phone
actions.feedbackWrong: Nothing on your phone is more urgent than the casualty in front of you.

actions.label: Take a selfie with the casualty
actions.feedbackWrong: Please don't. Privacy and dignity apply in a disaster too.

actions.label: Look for snacks
actions.feedbackWrong: Eat at the rest break, not mid-sieve.

actions.label: Post an update on social media
actions.feedbackWrong: Information goes through the incident controller, not your socials.
